newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Commodity markets, A$ seen firming - Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Commodity markets, A$ seen firming - Dresdner.

text.p: Dresdner Australia Ltd expects a firming in commodity prices in the first half of 1997, chief economist Rob Henderson told a commodities conference on Monday.
The outlook for G7 economies is for growth to remain relatively robust, he told the Asia-Pacific Commodity Markets conference in Sydney.
There was ground for optimism Japan may outperform the 1997 forecast of 1.9 percent GDP growth set by Consensus Economics which would lift the G7 growth profile of 2.4 percent, he said.

"In our view, the ongoing robust performance of the global economy is consistent with a further upswing in commodity prices, averaging about 4-5 percent between now and the middle of 1997," Henderson said.
This would be consistent with a rise in the Australian dollar to about 82.5 U.S. cents, he said.
However, he said it seemed likely that commodity markets would swing down in the second half of 1997 as they anticipated the peak in global production.
This implied that the Australian dollar would then fall back to U.S. 80 cents and lower into 1998, he said.
Non-Japan Asia was now the most important commodity export destination in the world, Henderson said.
Overall, a gentle upswing in commodity trade was expected to continue, supporting the Australian dollar, he said.
